title: Terms of a Rental Agreement
text:
A rental agreement is a legal contract between a landlord and a tenant. It sets out the rights and duties of both parties, including the amount of rent and the date it must be paid. The contract also states how long the lease will last. If either party breaks a term of the agreement, the other party may be entitled to compensation.

Many agreements include a clause that allows the tenant to end the lease early. However, the tenant usually has to give written notice, often one or two months in advance. In some cases, a penalty must be paid for leaving early. Before signing, a tenant should read every clause carefully and ask for an explanation of any term that is unclear.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does a rental agreement set out?
options: The rights and duties of both parties
The price of the building only
The rules of the local courts

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what must a tenant usually give before ending a lease early?
options: The name of a new tenant

questions.text: What can be inferred about why a tenant should read every clause before signing?
options: Clauses are usually written in a foreign language
Some terms may have consequences the tenant does not expect
Landlords refuse to sign with tenants who ask questions
Contracts are only valid if they are very short

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about a clause that allows a tenant to end a lease early?
options: It makes the lease impossible to end
It is always free of cost for both parties
It may come with conditions, such as a penalty or a notice period
It is required by law in every country

paragraph_translations: Um contrato de aluguel é um acordo jurídico entre um senhorio e um inquilino. Ele estabelece os direitos e deveres das duas partes, incluindo o valor do aluguel e a data em que deve ser pago. O contrato também informa por quanto tempo a locação vai durar. Se uma das partes descumprir alguma condição do acordo, a outra pode ter direito a indenização.

Muitos acordos incluem uma cláusula que permite ao inquilino encerrar a locação antecipadamente. No entanto, o inquilino geralmente precisa dar aviso por escrito, muitas vezes com um ou dois meses de antecedência. Em alguns casos, é necessário pagar uma multa para sair antes do prazo. Antes de assinar, o inquilino deve ler cada cláusula com atenção e pedir explicação sobre qualquer termo pouco claro.
